messages:
eli.wong (customer): Hey team -- we've started getting a burst of 429s this morning from our backend. Same client, same key, nothing changed on our side. Example response headers we got in one failed request:

X-RateLimit-Scope: org
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
Retry-After: 45
X-Request-ID: rwd-abc123

We believe our project quota isn't exhausted (we checked Dashboard -> Project -> Usage), so not sure why org scope would be hit. Any ideas?

alyssa.chen (support): Sorry you're seeing that, Eli. A few quick clarifying Qs: 1) Are you calling directly from your servers or through a customer-managed proxy / CDN? 2) Do you have multiple projects or services sharing a single org-level API key? 3) Can you paste the Authorization header pattern (you can redact the token)?

eli.wong (customer): We're behind an internal proxy (envoy) that does connection pooling. We do rotate keys for blue/green deploys but each service should be using the project key. Authorization header looks like: `Authorization: Bearer proj_live_XXXX` (project-scoped). We also saw the rate-limiter-bot message in the logs: `rate-limiter-bot: quota exceeded (ip: 18.205.34.12)` 

alyssa.chen (support): Thanks — that `rate-limiter-bot` line is interesting. If the proxy is pooling requests and sending them from a small set of egress IPs, IP-based buckets (shared across multiple API keys from the same IP) can be exhausted even if individual keys are fine. Two quick repro/debug steps: 1) curl directly from one of your backend machines with the project key to see headers. 2) run `curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer proj_live_XXXX" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` and paste headers.

eli.wong (customer): Ran step 1 from one app host, small test request returned: 

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-RateLimit-Scope: project
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 998
X-Request-ID: rwd-abc126

So direct calls show project scope. Calls through the proxy show org scope and 0 remaining. Proxy egress IP is 18.205.34.12. Not sure why scope flips to org when forwarded through the proxy.

marc.rivera (eng-infra): Quick note: the server will surface the most restrictive applicable limit in the response headers. If our gateway detects requests that cannot be attributed to a single project (for example, because the Authorization header is missing or malformed after proxy rewriting) it may fallback to an org-scoped bucket for that IP. Two possibilities: 1) proxy removes or mangles the Authorization header for some requests; 2) proxy is fronting multiple projects but using an org-level token for healthchecks or admin probes, consuming org quota. Can you capture a raw request sample (headers) for a failing proxy request?

eli.wong (customer): Attaching a redacted raw request we captured from the proxy (pasted):

:method: POST
:scheme: https
:authority: api.redwood.example
:path: /v1/generate
content-type: application/json
authorization: BEARER proj_live_XXXX  <-- note uppercase BEARER, token OK
x-forwarded-for: 203.0.113.45, 18.205.34.12

Would uppercase "BEARER" cause attribution mismatch?

zara.patel (eng-sre): Good catch. Auth parsing should be case-insensitive for the scheme per RFC, but we have seen proxies that insert extra whitespace or unusual header encodings that can trip our attribution heuristics. Another angle: if the proxy strips or rewrites the header for some probe requests (e.g., health check to /v1/ping) and those probes happen frequently, they may be charged to the org or IP bucket depending on how the request reaches our edge. Could you grep proxy configs for any healthcheck routes that might be using a different token? Also check whether your proxy normalizes header casing (it shouldn't break the token).

eli.wong (customer): We found an internal admin script that does `curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer "` (empty bearer) during a periodic test — oops. That would strip project attribution.

marc.rivera (eng-infra): That explains the org scope. Empty/malformed Authorization + same egress IP -> requests get attributed to the IP/org bucket. Two remediation steps: 1) stop the admin test or give it a proper project key; 2) if you need to continue proxying many projects through the same IP, request an IP-level burst increase from support or enable per-project routing via separate egress IPs.

alyssa.chen (support): I'll flag this to Billing/Quota team to see if we can clear any transient penalties on the org bucket and remove the Retry-After penalties. Can you paste the `X-Request-ID` from one of the org-scoped 429s? That helps us find the exact server side logs (you already pasted `rwd-abc123` earlier).

eli.wong (customer): rwd-abc123 was from the 429. Thanks.

rate-limiter-bot: Note: org bucket "acme-corp" hit soft limit 45m ago; automatic backoff policy applied for 60s windows.

marc.rivera (eng-infra): Logged an internal trace for `rwd-abc123` and confirmed a sequence of malformed auth requests from IP 18.205.34.12 starting at 08:12 UTC. Those were charging the org bucket. We recommended removing the errant admin probe and reissuing a project key while you confirm the proxy normalization config.

alyssa.chen (support): Follow-ups we took on our side:
- Opened a short-term lift on org bucket for 10 minutes to let you drain queued traffic (ID: QL-9921).
- Noted for quota team to send you a one-time compensatory credit for retries.

eli.wong (customer): We stopped the admin test and switched the admin script to use a designated monitoring key. After that, traffic through the proxy shows project-scoped headers again: 

X-RateLimit-Scope: project
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 997
X-Request-ID: rwd-abc140

Looks resolved from our side. Thanks for the quick help.

zara.patel (eng-sre): For long-term: recommend one of the following depending on your architecture: 
- Use SNAT pools / multiple egress IPs per project so IP buckets aren't shared.
- Prefer per-project egress (one IP per service) where feasible.
- Use distinct API keys for non-prod vs prod and for monitoring probes so they don't consume prod project quota.
- Consider Redwood Dedicated if you need guaranteed throughput without org-level sharing.

marc.rivera (eng-infra): Also adding a small change to attribution heuristics: if Authorization header appears but is empty or `Bearer` is present without token, we will mark it as malformed but won't attribute to org bucket immediately — instead mark as 'unattributed' and rate-limit at a higher fallback threshold. I'll open a PR and add a note in eng-infra.

alyssa.chen (support): Glad this was quick. I'll keep QL-9921 open for one hour in case you see any regression; please @mention me if it reappears. :tada:

eli.wong (customer): Thanks everyone! Confirming all good now. :white_check_mark:
